In 2019, during my MSc in Geoinformatics, I made a set of maps of Andros. I gathered the base data from free online sources, built the digital terrain models myself and designed two printed 1:150,000 maps: one with contours, one with hypsometric tints and hillshading. There was also a web version, served through GeoServer with OpenLayers on top.

It worked, but it needed a running map server, styling files for every layer and someone to keep it all alive. That's fine for a course. It's not realistic for a small island.

![The rebuilt map: relief from the 13 m terrain model, settlements, beaches, churches and the road network](screenshot-island.png)

## What was missing

Before rebuilding anything, I looked at what's already out there. The Municipality of Andros publishes its maps as static images. The best interactive maps of the island come from others: [Andros Routes](https://www.androsroutes.gr/), a non-profit, maintains the trail network, and commercial publishers sell hiking maps. What I couldn't find was a simple, free map of the whole island that also speaks the coordinate system local engineers work in, the Greek Grid (ΕΓΣΑ87).

## The map

The new version is a single web page, with no server behind it:

- **Relief first.** The 13 m terrain model and hillshade are blended into one relief image, so the island's shape reads at a glance.
- **Names that suit the zoom.** The generalised 1:150,000 settlements from 2019 decide which village names appear when you're zoomed out, so that generalisation work still has a job.
- **Click anywhere** for the elevation and the coordinates in both WGS84 and ΕΓΣΑ87.
- **Draw a route** for its length, ascent, descent and an elevation profile.
- **Greek and English**, with search that ignores accents, and its own symbol for every kind of feature.
- **Optional OpenStreetMap layers** for day-to-day use: health centres, pharmacies, police and fire stations, municipal offices, fuel, bus stops, springs, viewpoints and the waymarked trails. Each trail opens its own elevation profile.

![Elevation profile from Chora across the island's central ridge](screenshot-profile.png)

## How I built it

I rebuilt it in Python: GeoPandas for the vector layers, rasterio for the terrain, and Leaflet for the map, using Claude as coding helper.

## What's next

I'd like to offer it to the Municipality of Andros as a starting point. Because it's one file, it can sit inside their existing website with a single line of code.

**Map:** [etymo.co.uk/AndrosWebMap](https://etymo.co.uk/AndrosWebMap/) · **Code:** [github.com/eritrouib/AndrosWebMap](https://github.com/eritrouib/AndrosWebMap)
